premises.text: Mobile users everywhere overpay and tolerate poor signal and call quality
premises.evidence_span: people pay too much for their mobile phone service. It costs too much money to make a phone call or to send a text message

premises.text: TextFree provides free, unlimited text messaging
premises.evidence_span: TextFree lets you send free, unlimited text messages

premises.text: Handing out real mobile numbers turns iPod Touches and iPads into communication platforms
premises.evidence_span: They were iPod touches, they were iPads. They turned them into communication platforms

premises.text: Day-one user behavior shows demand for voice calling
premises.evidence_span: aside from sending what can only be described as an assload of text messages, half of them got a phone call

premises.text: TextFree with Voice is a full SIP-based VoIP client that makes free calls
premises.evidence_span: Text-free with voice is a full-on SIP-based voice over IP client. It turns your iPod Touch, iPad into a phone, lets you make free phone calls

premises.text: Target users are 12 to 26 years old and do not pay for things
premises.evidence_span: Now, our users are between 12 and 26 years old. We've got over 8 million of them. They don't pay for anything.

premises.text: Offer-wall economics let users earn free minutes while app makers get downloads and Pinger gets paid
premises.evidence_span: user gets free minutes. The company gets the download, and they go up in the iTunes charts, and we get paid

premises.text: The post-send waiting moment is premium ad inventory for brands courting young users
premises.evidence_span: it's a perfect time for an ad. And brands want to connect with our users because our users are making brand decisions for the first times in their lives

domains.name: Costly mobile service for price-sensitive young users
Free text and voice over data

value.text: Free, high-quality unlimited texting and talking for users who could never pay
value.evidence_span: our customers could literally never pay for a very, very high quality phone service that gives them unlimited texting and unlimited talking

causal_links.evidence_span: they don't have a lot of money to spend on things like this. So now what you could do is you could go to our offer window
people pay too much for their mobile phone service
lets you make free phone calls

notes: Partition is a need/product/money triad; justified because the monetization engine (offer wall plus ad inventory) can be revised without touching the SIP client ('user gets free minutes... we get paid' is a separate economics claim), and the segment and pain assumptions are separately learnable. Message counts, number handouts, 8M users, and 1.3B impressions treated as traction with mechanisms coded instead; in-flight and Facebook extensions folded as platform roadmap items (v1.3.2 4.1(5)).
